title: Corpus-driven matcher smoke spec: assert every wildcard_corpus matches[] is true + non_matches[] is false in BOTH namespaces
description: Fowler-reviewer PR-D note: both Wild::Analyzers::Permission and Wild::CapabilityGate MUST load lib/wild/schemas/wildcard_corpus.yml at boot and run a smoke spec asserting every entry's matches[] returns true and every non_matches[] returns false against their matcher. This is the contract test that converts PR-D from 'shared data' to 'anti-drift fence.' Without it F4 is paper. Special case: negation entries (!User::Admin) have matches: [] by design — smoke harness needs an explicit branch to skip the matches[] loop and only assert non_matches[]. Source: martin-fowler-reviewer Gate 1 sign-off on PR #15.

title: Resolve Wild.config.admin_tools.{cache,job,flag}_adapter :default sentinels at Wild::Engine after_initialize
description: Fowler-reviewer Gate 1 callout on PR-B (#12): the typed Wild::Configuration leaves admin_tools adapters as :default sentinel values to preserve Karpathy transport-host independence (no Rails.cache / ActiveJob::Base / Flipper at require time). The engine MUST resolve these in Wild::Engine.config.after_initialize: if cache_adapter == :default and defined?(Rails.cache), set Rails.cache; same for ActiveJob::Base; Flipper only if defined?(Flipper). Leaving the sentinel un-resolved at request time will surface as NoMethodError on Symbol#fetch in production. Owner: Role 5 (admin_tools move) coordinating with Role 4 (engine boot). Source: Fowler review comment on PR #12 + 000-docs/003-AT-ARCH-architecture.md § Configuration shape.

title: F5: Downgrade Wild::Skillops claims to match what the code can actually back up

Resolution inside the consolidation: inline as Wild::Skillops internal namespace; remove all atomicity/durability claims; default config.skillops.enabled = false. Earn separate gem (ADR-0002) when a real consumer appears with proven need. Source: /home/jeremy/000-projects/wild/wild-rails-ai-ops/000-docs/013-AT-AUDT-thinker-council-verdict-rev2-2026-05-29.md

title: F3: Replace vanity test counts with judgment tests across all namespaces
description: Council rev2 §F3. Beck explicit; Karpathy implicit (transport tests, no agent evals); Armstrong implicit (no audit-liveness probe); Lamport, Huyen concur. Today the old gems brag about test counts; many tests assert code runs without asserting judgment is correct. Resolution: characterization tests against captured behavior; golden corpora for classifiers; audit-liveness probes; agent-eval seams in bin/eval. NOT a count metric. Test count is forbidden as a quality claim. Source: /home/jeremy/000-projects/wild/wild-rails-ai-ops/000-docs/013-AT-AUDT-thinker-council-verdict-rev2-2026-05-29.md

title: F2: Make every CapabilityGate rescue emit a structured audit event; :evaluation_error is hard-fail
description: Council rev2 §F2. Armstrong's most-leveraged finding; Beck, Fowler, Kleppmann concur. Today the gate has rescue paths that silently swallow exceptions, leaving no audit trace. Fix: every rescue inside lib/wild/capability_gate/ emits a structured Wild::CapabilityGate audit event with outcome: :evaluation_error AND denies the request. Evidence required: audit-liveness spec deliberately corrupts policy fixture and asserts both event emission and outcome=:deny. See schemas/capability_gate/audit_event.yml for shape. Source: /home/jeremy/000-projects/wild/wild-rails-ai-ops/000-docs/013-AT-AUDT-thinker-council-verdict-rev2-2026-05-29.md

title: Reconcile Wild::AdminTools::Configuration (nil-default injection points) with the central Wild::Configuration::AdminTools :default sentinels at engine boot
description: Role 5 PR-12 (wild-rvv.3) moved wild-admin-tools-mcp into Wild::AdminTools behavior-preservingly, KEEPING the gem's Configuration as Wild::AdminTools::Configuration (settings: cache_adapter, job_adapter, flag_adapter, gate, policy_path, audit_log_path, audit_store — all nil-default = dependency-injection points) plus the module-level Wild::AdminTools.configuration accessor. NOT folded into the central Wild::Configuration::AdminTools typed struct, which PR-B set with cache/job/flag = :default sentinels (for Karpathy transport-independence + F2). Two reasons it's deferred: (1) the gem has 4 attrs the central struct lacks (gate, policy_path, audit_log_path, audit_store); (2) the gem's code/tests treat nil adapters as 'not configured', while :default means 'resolve to Rails.cache/ActiveJob/Flipper at boot' — reconciling these IS the 'kill the DI container' adapter-defaulting work. This overlaps wild-rvv.3.1 (admin_tools adapter sentinel resolution at Wild::Engine after_initialize). Role 8 task: at engine boot, resolve central :default sentinels to real adapters AND bridge them into the Wild::AdminTools::Configuration the gem's pipeline reads (or unify the two configs). Until then, Wild::AdminTools.configuration works standalone with injected adapters (behavior identical to old gem). Parallels introspection's wild-rvv.u16. Source: Role 5 PR-12 move decision + canonical decision #5 (DI container is dead, adapters defaulted in lib/wild/admin_tools/).

title: Wire Wild.config.introspection.access_policy_path into the Wild::Introspection::Configuration policy loader at engine boot
description: Role 5 PR-11 (wild-rvv.2) moved wild-rails-safe-introspection-mcp into Wild::Introspection behavior-preservingly, KEEPING the gem's rich Configuration class as Wild::Introspection::Configuration (a YAML policy loader with blocked_columns_for/allowed_models/etc.) plus the module-level Wild::Introspection.configuration accessor. This is intentionally NOT folded into the central Wild::Configuration::Introspection typed struct (which holds access_policy_path + allowed_models per PR-B), because the gem's Configuration does real work (loads access_policy.yml, resolves per-model blocked columns) — collapsing it would be a behavior change. Parallels the admin_tools adapter-resolution pattern (wild-rvv.3.1). Role 6/8 task: at Wild::Engine after_initialize, when Wild.config.introspection.access_policy_path is set, construct/refresh the Wild::Introspection::Configuration policy loader from it so the engineer configures via the central block and the introspection runtime reads the loaded policy. Until then, Wild::Introspection.configuration works standalone (behavior identical to the old gem). Source: Role 5 PR-11 move decision.

title: Pin the Evaluator-never-raises contract with a Gate-rescue test (Armstrong F2 fast-follow)
description: joe-armstrong-reviewer SIGN on Role 6 PR-1 (F2, wild-rvv.4.1) with fast-follow findings. The Gate#evaluate outer rescue (deny_with_error) is audit-blind BY CONSTRUCTION — the Gate holds no audit writer; emission lives in the Evaluator. Today this is safe because Evaluator#evaluate never raises (it has its own rescue that emits + denies). But that invariant is unguarded: if a future refactor removes the Evaluator's rescue, the Gate's outer rescue becomes a silent audit-blind denial — the exact F2 hole displaced one layer up. Finding 2 (P2): add a Gate-level spec that forces the evaluator to raise (allow_any_instance_of(Wild::CapabilityGate::Evaluator).to receive(:evaluate).and_raise) and asserts Gate#evaluate still returns denied + reason :evaluation_error. The deny_with_error doc comment pinning this was already added in PR-1; this bead is the matching test. Finding 4 (optional hardening): log_audit_failure interpolates error.message — a pathological exception whose #message raises would degrade a should-have-logged into terminal silence; consider interpolating error.class first, error.message in a nested guarded fragment. Source: Armstrong F2 sign-off, Role 6 PR-1. Findings 3 (both-broken terminal-silence 9th/10th liveness examples) + the deny_with_error comment already landed in PR-1.
